item.title: Implement safe_extract.py from SPEC with boundary tests
item.brief: Implement safe_extract.py exactly according to SPEC.md, preserving the documented extract(entries, root) API. Add focused tests beyond existing basics for every specified validation error and boundary case, especially non-list batches without consumption, malformed entries/types, unsafe POSIX path forms/components, duplicates and file/directory collisions in either order, invalid roots, symlink/dangling symlink and non-directory ancestors/targets, pre-existing targets, and validation failures leaving root/outside unchanged. Ensure valid batches preserve input order and exact bytes, support missing nested directories/empty files, and empty batches validate root. Use Python standard library only. Run focused test suite. Commit the completed work as requested.

evidence.caption: Focused unittest suite on the final committed implementation

pr.body: safe_extract.py validates list-only batches, tuple and value types, POSIX path forms, duplicate/collision rules, root and existing path components without following symlinks, and absent targets before creating directories or files. Writes use exclusive creation. test_safe_extract.py covers invalid batches and roots, path boundaries, conflicts in either order, symlink/dangling-link and non-directory cases, no-mutation failures, input order, exact bytes, nested directories, empty files, and empty batches. Verification: python3 -m unittest -v (9 passed); git diff --check (passed). Three reviewers read base 9014ad80fa6a5d5f73ada09d55d997faa312d281 through d3eaae9672dd068b52acb20bfd36b03e7031854b and passed with no findings. Assumes the stable filesystem specified by SPEC.md; concurrent changes and rollback after I/O errors are outside scope.
pr.summary: Implemented safe extraction for validated regular-file batches. Before: extract was unimplemented; now batches are checked before filesystem changes and valid files are written in order with exact bytes.
